title: Warped-sigmoid Poisson-process mixed-effects models (WSPmm)
text: Wispack (pronounced “wisp package” “wisp pack”) R package testing -group effects spatial variation spatial transcriptomics data. variation often functional, can thought functional spatial effects (FSE). True-color image fluorescing probes bound mRNA molecules cortical cells, raw data spatial transcriptomics. Unlike testing spatially variable genes (SVGs), involves testing spatial variation gene expression within group, unlike differential expression (DE) analysis tests -group effects without regard spatial distribution, testing FSEs involves testing whether factor age rearing conditions nonzero effect spatial variation groups differing factor. Comparison testing differentially expressed genes, spatially variable genes, genes function spatial effects. visualization purposes, mouse brain slices represent tissue sample laterality (left vs right hemisphere) represents fixed effect (.e., covariate). Wispack performs FSE testing first using change-point detection find spatial variation samples, fitting nonlinear mixed-effect model detected change points. core nonlinear model parameterization found change-points inflections logistic functions representing gradients gene expression change. Multiple change-points handled summing component logistic functions “poly-sigmoid” function. Fixed effects (age rearing conditions) modeled effects underlying logistic parameters. Random (within group) effects modeled nonlinear warping poly-sigmoid. Significance testing performed effects either bootstrapping MCMC resampling. complete mathematical description wisp models can found paper, applied details covered tutorials site. (See “Articles” link navigation bar.) Demo plots functions involved wisp. () logistic function, used model single change point gene expression. (B) wisp poly-sigmoid function, built three logistic components, representing three change points. (C) warping function used represent random effects, e.g., variation due differences individual animals due measurement noise. (D) wisp poly-sigmoid (B) warping function applied. Wispack provides user-facing function, wisp, takes data frame familiar format expected standard R functions linear models (e.g., lme4::lmer stats::lm) runs complete test FSEs. Preprocessing data generally required passing wisp, wisp executes pipeline involving parameter estimates, prediction, model fitting, hypothesis testing. Note version 2.2, wisp includes option (LRO_cost, model.settings) perform grid search best settings change-point detection (LRO) search, “best” defined either lowest AIC, BIC, negative log-likelihood. Top-level overview wisp modeling pipeline. shown figure , steps pipeline nonlinear recurrent. Full modeling pipeline wisp. Boxes represent variables model, operations performed variables. Unlike standard linear modeling packages R require model formula, wisp merely needs data. example, quick-start demo (uses data mice RORB expression across laminar axis primary somatosensory cortex) runs following code: model formula required. default, wisp models include possible effect interactions. However, version 2.1, effect interactions can removed model using trtKO argument model.settings. , set defaults, column names data must associated model variables using variables argument. example: quick-start demo another demo showing model options can run using demo() command: tutorials provide detailed walkthroughs package options: Poisson processes sigmoids: Introduction wisps parameterize model spatial distribution count data Poisson process gene transcription. title: Function to analyze benchmark results from attractor-based simulations — analyze_attractor_sim_benchmarks
text: function analyzes results benchmarking modeling methods attractor-based simulation datasets. computes performance metrics: correlation coefficients rate random effect parameters, false positive rates (FPR), false discovery rates (FDR), power spatially variable gene (SVG) functional spatial effect (FSE) parameters. FPR, FDR, power defined follows: FP: p-value \(\alpha\) true null effect TN: p-value \(\alpha\) true null effect TP: p-value \(\alpha\) true non-null effect FN: p-value \(\alpha\) true non-null effect FPR: FP / (FP + TN) FDR: FP / (FP + TP) Power: TP / (TP + FN) exact interpretation depend returned modeling functions used. example, model_attractor_simulation_wisp returns p-values rate-effect parameter returns "FSE" parameter type, FPR, FDR, power "FSE" parameter type computed based rate-effect estimates .

text: function benchmarks provided list modeling methods attractor-based simulation datasets. simulates data multiple times, fits modeling method simulated data, records results computation times step.

title: Function to run benchmarks on attractor-based simulations — run_attractor_sim_benchmarks
code: run_attractor_sim_benchmarks(   seed_data,   n_sims = 100,   n_bins = 100,   n_replicates = 4,   replicate_spatial_scalar = 0.05,   min_effect_size = 0.05,   modeling_functions = list(wisp = model_attractor_simulation_wisp),   modeling_function_args = list(wisp = list(bs_num = 1000, max_fork = 1)) )

title: Function to run benchmarks on attractor-based simulations — run_attractor_sim_benchmarks
text: seed_data data frame containing seed dataset columns: gene, coord_x, coord_y, count. given attractor_simulation generate simulations. n_sims integer specifying number simulations run. Default 100. n_bins integer specifying number spatial bins divide data coordinates simulation. Default 100. n_replicates integer specifying number replicates generate treatment condition simulation. Default 4. replicate_spatial_scalar numeric value controlling amount spatial variation introduced replicate simulation. Default 0.05. min_effect_size numeric value specifying minimum effect size functional spatial effects (FSEs) simulation. Default 0.05. Max positive effect size always 4, .e., 4x change rate. max min effect size, .e., effect can drop rate zero. modeling_functions named list modeling functions benchmark. function take least arguments sim (simulation object produced attractor_simulation) sim_num (simulation number). Default list containing model_attractor_simulation_wisp function. Functions provided list return dataframe columns est, true, param, id, method, sim. true column contain, simulation applicable parameter, ground-truth value returned attractor_simulation_ground_truth function. est column contain corresponding estimated value modeling function. param column contain name parameter (one "rate_effect", "random_effect", "FSE", "SVG"). id column contain name gene replicate associated parameter. method column contain name modeling method used. sim column contain simulation number. modeling_function_args named list lists, sub-list contains additional arguments pass corresponding modeling function modeling_functions. Default list containing arguments model_attractor_simulation_wisp function.

title: Function to run benchmarks on attractor-based simulations — run_attractor_sim_benchmarks
text: list containing two components: results, data frame compiling results simulations modeling methods; times, data frame recording computation times data simulation modeling method simulation.

code: wisp(   count.data,   variables = list(),   fit_only = FALSE,   use.median = FALSE,   bootstraps.num = 0,   converged.resamples.only = TRUE,   max.fork = 1,   verbose = TRUE,   model.settings = list(),   MCMC.settings = list(),   plot.settings = list(),   ran.seed = 1234 )

title: Fit wisp to count data — wisp
text: count.data Data.frame, data modeled, columns model variables (count, bin, context, species, ran, fixedeffects), equivalent variables specified variables argument. variables List, names columns count.data correspond model variables. list contain (necessarily ) named elements: count, bin, context, species, ran, timeseries, fixedeffects. fit_only Logical, TRUE, fits model full data set using L-BFGS returns fitted model without running resampling (MCMC bootstrapping); FALSE, runs MCMC /bootstrapping estimate parameter uncertainty. use.median Logical, TRUE, median resamples used final parameter estimates; FALSE, fit L-BFGS full, original data used. bootstraps.num Integer, number bootstrap resamples perform. 0, MCMC run. converged.resamples.Logical, TRUE, resamples converged fit used statistical analysis; FALSE, resamples used. Applies bootstraps. max.fork Integer, maximum number parallel processes use bootstrapping. Applies Mac Linux. Must 1 windows. verbose Logical, TRUE, prints information fitting process. model.settings List, settings C++ model, including: buffer_factor = 0.05: minimum distance t-points must proportion max_bin. ctol = 1e-6: Convergence tolerance L-BFGS. max_penalty_at_distance_factor = 0.01: Maximum penalty applied negative log-likelihood non-trivial distance parameter bounds. LRO_cost = "AIC": Character string giving cost function use evaluating likelihood-ratio outlier (LRO) parameters testing expression-rate transition points data ("AIC", "BIC", "NLL"; anything else defaults hand-specified LROcutoff LROwindow_factor). LROcutoff = 2.0: Cutoff used LROcp_find function, multiple standard deviation. Specifically, point evaluated ratio likelihood data model transition point likelihood data model without change point. point taken transition point ratio number standard deviations mean across points. LROwindow_factor = 1.25: controls size window used LROcp_find algorithm (window = LROwindow_factor X bin_num X buffer_factor) rise_threshold_factor = 0.8: Amount detected rise fraction total required end run making initial estimates transition-point slopes. max_evals = 1000: Maximum number evaluations optimization, using L-BFGS. rng_seed = 42: Seed random number generator used internal C++. warp_precision = 1e-7: Decimal precision retain selecting really big number pseudo infinity unbound warping. round_none = TRUE: Logical specifying whether round extrapolated counts "none" (random effect) nearest integer. trtKO = c("none"): List effect names remove model, e.g., model without Factor1 x Factor2 interaction. Must match one treatment levels full model. max_bin = 0.0: Largest bin number; left zero, infer count data MCMC.settings List, settings MCMC simulation, including: MCMC.burnin = 1e2: Number random-walk steps take find optimal parameters. zero, start walk L-BFGS parameters. MCMC.steps = 1e3: Number random-walk steps take resampling parameters. MCMC.step.size = 0.5: Standard deviation normal distribution controlling random-walk step size. MCMC.prior = 1.0: Prior compute Bayesian update controlling step acceptance. MCMC.neighbor.filter = 1: save every -many steps resample. plot.settings List, settings plots make, including: print.plots = TRUE: Logical indicating whether print plots produced model fit. dim.bounds = Vector bins; non-empty, rate-count plots plot vertical dot-dashed lines coordinates indicate prior-known boundary along spatial dimension. Note values used way model fit . log.scale = False: Logical indicating whether plots show log expression-rate values (plus 1). splitting_factor = c(): Name fixed-effect factor. Must either empty length 1. provided, rate-count time-series plots determine color hue treatment levels value fixed-effect level. Within splitting factor levels, fixed-effect factor level determines color brightness. Note splitting-factor color scheme effect exactly two fixed-effect levels (one can time series, splitting factor time series). CI_style = TRUE: Logical indicating whether rate-count plots show (TRUE:) predicted treatment-level expression rates free individual effects plus shading showing 95% confidence invervals, (FALSE:) observed data points, plus fitted treatment-level expression rates individual samples predictions free individual effects. splitting_factor_colors = c(120, 240): Vector two integers (range 0:360) giving hue level splitting factor. label_size, title_size, axis_size, legend_size, count_size: Controls plot element sizes. count_jitter = 0.5: Scale jitter apply plotting data given input. count.alpha.ran, count.alpha.none, pred.alpha.ran, pred.alpha.none: Controls plot element alpha-levels. ran.seed = 1234: Integer, random seed reproducibility. Used within R. NULL, seed set. Default 1234.

title: Fit wisp to count data — wisp
text: List giving results fitted model, including: model.component.list = "Rt", "tslope", "tpoint": Character vector giving main model components; always "Rt" = rate, "tslope" = transition-point slope, "tpoint" = transition-point location. count.data.summed: Data frame fitted data. one row per combination spatial bin, fixed effects, random effects. Contains columns bin, count (sum spots given species label), pred (predicted rate), count.log log count, plus one, pred.log (log predicted rate plus one), context, species, ran (random-effect level), treatment (treatment level). fitted.parameters: Vector fitted model parameters. gamma.disperson: Matrix giving estimated gamma dispersion gamma-convolved Poisson model. param.names: Names model parameters, matching order fitted.parameters. fix: List containing four elements: names (names fixed-effect factors), lvls (list, element names levels fixed-effect factor), treat.lvl (, excluding reference levels), ref.lvl (, containing reference-level). treatment: List two elements: names (names treatment levels) components (list, element names fixed-effect factor levels constituting treatment level). grouping.variables: List containing character vectors context.lvls, species.lvls, ran.lvls holding, respectively, grouping levels context, species, random-effect grouping variabes. param.idx0: List containing zero-indexed index values fitted.parameters different combinations treatment levels grouping factors. settings: copy original model settings provided wisp function. sample.params.type: character string, "bs" "MCMC", specifies type resamples used compute stats. sample.params.bs: data frame giving resampled parameters bootstrapping (). sample.params.MCMC: data frame giving resampled parameters MCMC resampling (). diagnostics.bs: Diagnostic information bootstrap resample. diagnostics.MCMC: Diagnostic information MCMC random-walk step (.e., resample). stats: List containing main data frame parameters results (p-values, estimate, confidence intervals, etc) statistical analysis model parameters, plus data frames holding model residuals. plots: List containing whatever plots generated model fit.
